column1: # profile: curl -fsSL --compressed --max-time 90, no credentials, no POST
# Three-way comparison for the same three URLs (ScribeEntry1 / ScoutNist / ExecCapture):
# S073 raw: 74fc2e1ff9b1 / e49ef52267ea / 673f5d878217  -> all 47203 bytes, three different sha256
# S074 raw: 642591084fe9 / 389177cee332 / 337d67213c75  -> all 45351 bytes, three different sha256
# S075 raw: 793b2236efef / 7bf12d6d21b8 / 90b757583a37  -> all 42741 bytes, three different sha256
# S073/S074/S075 normalized: 950ae8a8ad88da31 / 955dd86653889462 / bb1cce593095f6c1 -> identical across all three fetches.
# Conclusion: the CSRC pages carry a fixed-size per-response marker; the rendered-text-v1
# normalized text is the reproducible identity, the raw body sha256 is not.
